3 . Name of the complainant : Sh. Dinesh  4. Date of Commission of Offence : 04.08.2015

5. Name and Parentage of Accused : 1. Jai Prakash  S/o Banke Lal R/o  House No. 55/56,
 Gali No. 10, Sainik  Enclave, Mohan  Garden, Delhi.
 2. Banke Lal S/o  Bhikam Singh, R/o  House no. 55/556,
 Gali no. 10, Sainik  Enclave, Mohan  Garden, Delhi.
 6. Offence complained of : U/s 498A/
 304B/34 IPC  7. Offence charged : Accused persons  charged  U/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.
 8. Plea of Guilt : Not guilty.
 9.

Final Order : Acquitted.
 10.

BRIEF FACTS AND REASONS FOR DECISION:
1.
The present FIR was registered on 05.10.2019 on the statement of Sh. Dinesh, brother of the deceased Harnesh.

As per the complaint Ex. PW-1/A, deceased Harnesh was married to accused Jai State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
1 Prakash @ Dev Prakash on 22.01.2019.

Rs. 4 Lacs were decided to be spent on the wedding but Rs.
3,50,000/- only were spent.
After 10 days of her marriage, when his sister had come for the ceremony of Dasai, her father in law accused Banke Lal told him that Rs. 50,000/- of the decided amount was balance.
He demanded the said amount as well as one ring, chain and motorcycle.
They could not fulfil the said demands due to money constraints, because of which husband and in laws of her sister started harrassing her.
His sister had told him in this regard on one or two occasions.
Lastly, when his sister Harnesh had visited him on Raksha Bandhan, she did not say anything in this regard.
On 03.10.2019, his sister Harnesh had called his elder sister Sunita and told her that she was only for 1-2 days.
There was no dispute between his sister Harnesh and her mother in law.

2. On the basis of this statement of Sh. Dinesh, brother of deceased Harnesh given before Ld. SDM,
Dwarka, present FIR was registered u/s 304B/498A/34 IPC as the deceased had expired an unnatural death on 04.10.2019 i.e. within 8 months of her marriage.
3. After completion of investigation, accused Jai Prakash, husband of deceased Harnesh and accused Banke Lal, her father in law were chargesheeted for offence u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.

CHARGE:
4. Detailed arguments were heard on charge from Ld. Counsel for accused persons and Ld.
Additional PP for State.
Vide order dated 16.12.2021, charges were framed u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC against both the accused persons who pleaded not guilty to the charges and claimed trial.

PROSECUTION EVIDENCE:
5. The prosecution led evidence and examined 9 Witnesses in all to bring home the guilt against the accused persons.
6. PW-1 Dinesh is the brother of deceased Harnesh and the complainant of the present case. PW-2 Hemraj is the father of deceased Harnesh and PW-3 Kalawati is the mother of deceased Harnesh.
7. All these three witnesses deposed in consonance with each other about the marriage between accused Jai Prakash @ Dev Prakash and deceased Harnesh in January, 2019.
They also deposed that they had spent Rs. 2-2.5 Lacs on the wedding ceremony and had given household articles in the marriage.
No jewellery was given at the time of marriage and Harnesh was living happily after the marriage.
8. They further deposed that on 04.10.2019, they had received a call that their daughter Harnesh had committed suicide.

They came to Delhi and identified her dead body vide statements Ex.
PW-1/B and Ex. PW-2/A.

Their statements were recorded before Ld. SDM which were proved as Ex.
PW-1/A, Ex. PW-2/B and Ex. PW-3/A.
They also deposed in consonance with each other that they were not aware about the reason because of which deceased Harnesh had committed suicide.
9. PW-1 identified the signatures on the arrest memo of accused Jai Prakash and Banke Lal which are Ex. PW-1/C and Ex. PW-1/D respectively.

State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
2 10.
PW-1 also deposed that prior to her marriage, her sister Harnesh used to tell him that she does not like accused Jai Prakash @Dev Prakash and they should not marry her to him.
11. All these witnesses were declared hostile and cross- examined on behalf of State.
They were confronted with their statement recorded before Ld. SDM but they failed to support the case of the prosecution.

12. PW-4 HC Pawan Kumar is a formal witness being the Duty Officer who proved the registration of the present FIR as Ex. PW-4/A and endorsement made on the rukka Ex. PW-4/B.
13.
PW-5 ASI
Devender Kumar is I/C Mobile Crime Team who had inspected the place of incident on 04.10.2019 vide his report Ex. PW-5/A.
He deposed that no suicide note was found at the spot.
14. PW-6 Ct.

Rupa Ram is a witness to the arrest of the accused persons vide memos Ex. PW-1/C and Ex. PW- 1/D and their disclosure statements Ex. PW-6/A and Ex.
PW-6/B.
15. PW-7 Ajit Singh Thakur is the then SDM, Dwarka who proved the recording of statements of Dinesh, brother of the deceased, Kalawati, mother of the deceased and Hemraj, father of the deceased by him which are Ex. PW- 1/A, Ex. PW-3/A and Ex. PW-2/B respectively.

ASI Harish Vats is the first IO who deposed about his visit to the spot on 04.10.2019 on receiving DD No. 64A, recording of the statement of the parental family members of the deceased by SDM Dwarka on 05.10.2019, seizure of the ligature material by him vide seizure memo Ex. PW-8/A and inspection of the spot by crime team.
He also deposed that post mortem of the dead body was conducted at DDU Hospital.
On the directions of SDM, he prepared the rukka and got the present FIR registered.

SI Prem Yadav is the second IO of the case who deposed about the arrest of accused persons vide memos Ex. PW-1/C and Ex. PW-1/D and recording of their disclosure statements Ex.
PW-6/A and Ex. PW-6/B.

He also deposed that during investigation, he prepared site plan Ex.
PW-9/A and after completion of investigation, he filed the chargesheet.
18.
In addition to the above evidence, accused persons admitted u/s 294 CrPC the photographs of the spot taken by the crime team, MLC No. 9083 of the deceased and the post mortem of the deceased.
Accordingly, the relevant witnesses to prove these documents were dropped from the list of witnesses.

STATEMENT OF ACCUSED:
19.

All the incriminating evidence that came on record in the deposition of the prosecution witnesses was put in detail to accused persons and their statements were recorded U/s. 313 CrPC on State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
They denied all the incriminating evidence and asserted that they were innocent and falsely implicated in the present case.
Deceased Harnesh was not happy with the marriage as she did not want to marry Jai Prakash and forced by her parents for the marriage.
At the time when she had committed suicide, none of the accused was present at the house and they were at their own workplaces.
After death of deceased, they came to know that deceased did not want to marry Jai Prakash.

DEFENCE EVIDENCE:
20. Accused persons did not lead any evidence in their defence.
21. Final arguments have been heard and record carefully perused.
JUDICIAL RESOLUTIONS:
22. It is a settled proposition of criminal law that prosecution is supposed to prove its case on the judicial file by leading cogent, convincing, reliable and trustworthy evidence beyond reasonable doubts.
The case of prosecution has to fall or stand on its own legs and it cannot derive the benefit from the weaknesses, if any, in the defence of the accused.

It is not for the accused to disprove the case of the prosecution and the onus to prove the case against the accused beyond reasonable doubts never shifts and always remains on the prosecution.
Further, benefit of doubt in the prosecution story always goes to the accused and it entitles the accused to acquittal.
23.

In the present case, accused persons are charged with the offences u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.
24.
Section 498A IPC provides punishment for cruelty to a woman by her husband or relative of her husband.
The term cruelty within the meaning of Section 498A IPC has been explained in the explanation to the said section.
It consists of two clauses (a) and (b).

To attract Section 498A IPC, it must be established that the cruelty or harassment to wife was to force her to cause grave bodily injury to herself or to commit suicide; or the harassment was to compel her to fulfill illegal demands of dowry.
Thus, every type of harassment or cruelty would not attract Section 498A IPC.

26. Section 304B IPC deals with dowry death and provides that where the death of a woman is caused, otherwise then under normal circumstances, within 7 years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death, she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry, such death shall be called dowry death and such husband or relative shall be deemed to have caused her death.
27.

Section 304B IPC mandates the drawing of a presumption that the husband or relative of the husband of the victim girl has caused her death and this presumption of dowry death corresponds to the presumption of dowry death as envisaged in Section 113B of the Evidence Act,
1872.
29. Section 304B IPC has two limbs.

The first defines the dowry death and the second, legal consequence of occurrence of dowry death i.e. husband or such other relative of husband who soon before the death of lady were found to have subjected her to cruelty or harassment shall conclusively be held to be guilty of the offence of dowry death.
Accordingly, where other ingredients of Section 304B IPC are satisfied, the husband or the relative shall be deemed to have caused the death of the lady.
In other words, the offence shall be deemed to have been committed by fiction of law.

Once the prosecution proves its case with regard to the basic ingredients of Section 304B IPC, the court will presume by deemed fiction of law that the husbands or the relatives complained of, have caused her death.
Such a presumption can be drawn by the court, keeping in view the evidence produced by the prosecution in support of the substantive charge u/s 304B IPC.

Undoubtedly, the deemed fiction would introduce a rebuttable presumption and the husband and relatives may, by leading their defence or proving that the ingredients of Section 304B were not satisfied, rebut the same.

State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
5 30.
The expression "soon before her death" used in Section 304B IPC cannot be given a restricted or a narrower meaning.

The legislative object in providing such a radius of time by employing the words, "soon before her death" is to emphasize the idea, that her death, in all probabilities, has been the aftermath of such cruelty or harassment.
In other words, there should be a reasonable, if not direct, nexus between her death and the dowry related cruelty or harassment inflicted upon her.
The demand for dowry should not be stale or an aberration of the past, but should be the continuing cause for the death u/s 304B IPC.

Neither the legislature nor the judicial pronouncements have put the terms "soon before her death" in a straight jacket formula by fixing any time for allotment and the interpretation of the same has been left to be determined by the Courts on the basis of the facts and circumstances of the case.
31. Section 304B IPC and Section 498A IPC are not mutually exclusive.
These provisions deal with two distinct offences, cruelty being a common essential to both the sections.
Explanation to Section 498A IPC gives meaning to the term cruelty, however, Section 304B IPC does not provide any explanation to this term.

However, considering the common background to these offences, the meaning of cruelty or harassment used in Section 304B IPC will be the same as given in explanation to Section 498A IPC under which "cruelty" by itself amounts to an offence and is punishable.
A person charged and acquitted for offence u/s 304B IPC can still be convicted u/s 498A IPC if its ingredients are proved on record.
32. Section 34 IPC provides exception to the general rule that no man can be held responsible for an independent act and wrong committed by another.
It lays down the principle of joint liability in the doing of a criminal act.
The essence of that liability is to be found in the existence of common intention, emanating from the accused leading to the doing of a criminal act in furtherance of such intention.

It deals with doing of separate acts, similar or adverse by several persons, if all are done in furtherance of common intention, each person is liable for the result thereof as if he had done the act himself.
The soul of Section 34 IPC is the joint liability of doing a criminal act.
This section only provides a rule of evidence and does not create a substantive offence.
Two elements are necessary to fulfill the requirement of Section 34 IPC.
One is that the person must be present on the scene of occurrence and the second is that there must be a prior concert or a pre- arranged plan.

Unless these two conditions are fulfilled, a person cannot be held guilty of an offence by operation of Section 34 IPC.
33.
Common intention implies a pre-arranged plan and acting in concert pursuance to that plan.
Common intention comes into being prior to the commission of act in point of time which need not be a long gap.
The common intention to give effect to a particular act may even develop at the spur of the moment between a number of persons with reference to the facts of a given case.
Where there is no direct evidence of common intention, it has to be inferred from circumstantial evidence.
34. Now, let us apply the above discussed definitions of the offences with which accused persons have been charged to the facts of the present case and evidence produced on record.

ARGUMENTS OF LD. DEFENCE COUNSEL:-
State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
6 35.It

is argued by Ld. Defence Counsel that on the basis of evidence that has been brought on record by the prosecution, it cannot be held that the conditions for invoking the presumption u/s 113-B Indian Evidence Act have been duly proved on record.
Accordingly, the presumption u/s 304-B IPC read with Section 113-B Indian Evidence Act cannot be invoked against the accused persons.

The parental family members of the deceased that are PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 have miserably failed to support the case of the prosecution regarding any kinds of dowry demands made by any of the accused persons or any harrassment given to the deceased on account of non- fulfilment of the said dowry demands.
Rather, they have clearly stated that the deceased was living happily in her matrimonial house after her marriage.

PW-1 Dinesh i.e. brother of the deceased has also admitted that prior to her marriage, deceased used to tell him that she does not like accused Jai Prakash @
Dev Prakash and they should not marry her to him.
As per the case of the accused persons also, the deceased was not happy in her marriage with accused Jai Prakash as she did not want to marry him and was forced by her parents into the marriage.
It is submitted that this might be the reason why deceased committed suicide on the fateful day.
However, there is no evidence on record to hold the accused persons guilty for the death of the deceased.
Accordingly, it is submitted that the accused persons are entitled to acquittal in the present case.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE STATE:
36.
Per contra, it is submitted by Ld.

Additional PP for the State that it has been duly proved on record that the death of deceased Harnesh was suicidal in nature and had taken place within three years of her marriage otherwise than under normal circumstances.

It has clearly come on record in the form of statements of paternal family members of the deceased recorded before the then SDM that are Ex. PW-1/A, Ex. PW-2/B and Ex. PW-3/A that she was harassed for various kinds of dowry demands prior to her demise.
These statements have been duly proved by the then SDM Dwarka who had recorded the statements and is examined as PW-7.
Even, PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 have not refused or denied having made these statements before the SDM.
Since, there are clear allegations of dowry demands in the statements of the parental family members of the deceased and these statements have been duly proved on record.
Accordingly, both the accused persons are liable for conviction for the offences charged against them.
FINDINGS:
37.I have heard the submissions made and carefully perused the record.
38. The accused persons have been charged for offences u/s 304B/498A IPC.
Dowry demands are an integral part of both these offences.
Accordingly, before proceeding further, it would be apposite to go through the evidence produced on record qua the allegations of dowry demands.
EVIDENCE QUA DOWRY DEMANDS:
39.It is the case of the prosecution that deceased Harnesh was subjected to cruelty and harassment on account of non- fulfilment of the dowry demands raised by the accused persons.

In order to prove the allegations in this regard, the prosecution is relying upon the statements of the parental family members of the deceased recorded before the then SDM Dwarka prior to registration of the present State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
7 FIR.

At the outset, it is noteworthy that these parental family members of the deceased that are her brother Dinesh, her father Hemraj and her mother Kalawati have been examined before this Court as PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 respectively but they have not supported the case of the prosecution regarding the dowry demands.

Although, all these three witnesses deposed about the marriage between deceased Harnesh and accused Jai Prakash and the money spent on the marriage but none of these witnesses made any allegations regarding any kinds of dowry demands made by the accused persons after marriage.
All these witnesses have been cross
- examined on behalf of the State but they did not support the case of the prosecution in this regard.
Ld. Additional PP for the State is relying upon their statements recorded before the then SDM, Dwarka which are Ex. PW-1/A, Ex. PW-2/B and Ex. PW-3/A respectively.

Although, these statements have been recorded prior to registration of present FIR and the allegations contained therein are not supported by PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3, still,
it would be apposite to go through these statements before giving any finding in the present case.

Perusal of these three statements show that only complainant Dinesh had made an allegation that when her sister Harnesh came to their house for the dasai ceremony, her father in law accused Banke Lal told them that Rs. 50,000/- was balance out of the money decided to be spent on the marriage and he demanded the said amount, one ring, one chain and one motorcycle.
On these demands, there were disputes between the families as they could not fulfil the demand and thereafter, her sister was harrassed by the accused persons.

He has also stated in his statement Ex.
PW-1/A, that his sister had told him once or twice about the harassment given to her.
However, he has not mentioned any date in this regard.
He has also stated in his statement Ex. PW-1/A that on 03.10.2019, her sister Harnesh had called her elder sister Sunita and told her that she was there only for only one or two days.
Interestingly, Sunita is neither cited as a witness in the present case nor her statement has been recorded during investigation and there are no call detail records to support these allegations.

Moreover, father of the deceased namely Hemraj and her mother Kalawati, in their statements Ex. PW-2/B and Ex. PW-3/A respectively had made no allegations of any kinds of dowry demands against the accused persons and have simply stated that they had spoken to their daughter Harnesh after marriage over telephone but she had not told them anything in this regard.

In these circumstances, even the allegations made by the complainant Dinesh in his statement Ex.
PW-1/A regarding the dowry demands are vague, without any specific date or time and without support of any corroborative evidence.

Even, the parents of the deceased have not supported the allegations of the said demands in their statements recorded before the then SDM which are Ex.
PW-2/B and Ex. PW-3/A.

In addition to this, the allegations contained in the statements of parental family members recorded before the then SDM, Dwarka are not supported by them in their testimonies recorded before Court as PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3.
40.

In view of the reasons given above, the evidence on record is highly insufficient for proving the fact that the deceased Harnesh was subjected to cruely and harassment on account of non-fulfillment of dowry demands raised by the accused persons.

41. Considering the overall evidence that has come on record, especially the depositions of PW-1,
PW-2 and PW-3, I have no hesitation in holding that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove on record beyond any reasonable doubt that any dowry demands were ever made by the accused persons from the deceased or her family members.

State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
8 42.

When the factum of dowry demands is not duly proved on record, the harassment of the deceased with a view to coerce her or any of her parental family members to meet the unlawful dowry demands have also not been proved on record beyond any reasonable doubt.

EVIDENCE QUA OFFENCE U/S 498A IPC:
43.As discussed above, in order to secure conviction for offence u/s 498A IPC, the prosecution is required to prove that the victim was subjected to cruelty by her husband or relatives of her husband either with a view to coerce her for meeting a demand of dowry or the cruelty was of such a nature as is likely to lead the lady to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her life, limb or health.
44.

In the present case, considering the above discussions and the overall evidence on record, I have no hesitation in holding that essential ingredients of Section 498A IPC have not been proved on record by the prosecution beyond any reasonable doubt.

Neither the demands of dowry are duly proved on record, nor it is proved on record that the harassment given to deceased Harnesh was of such a nature as was likely to drive her to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her life, limb or health.

Although, deceased Harnesh has committed suicide as per medical evidence, however, the evidence on record is highly deficient for holding that it was because of the cruelty suffered by her at the hands of any of the accused persons.
Admittedly, none of the accused persons were present along with the deceased Harnesh at the time of incident.
Accordingly, both the accused persons namely Jai Prakash @ Dev Prakash and Banke Lal are entitled to acquittal for offence u/s 498A/34 IPC.
EVIDENCE QUA OFFENCE UNDER SECTION 304B IPC:

45.As discussed above, Section 304B IPC mandates drawing of a presumption that husband or relatives of the husband of the victim girl had caused her death in case the essential ingredients provided by the Section are proved on record.
46.In the present case, it is duly proved on record that death of deceased Harnesh was caused in the circumstances which are not normal within 7 years from the date of her marriage.

However, the prosecution has miserably failed to prove on record that deceased Harnesh was subjected to cruelty or harassment for or in connection with any demands of dowry soon before her death by either of the accused persons.

47. Neither, PW-1 nor PW-2 or PW-3 have deposed about any incident to show that soon before her death, the deceased Harnesh was subjected to cruelty or harassment by any of the accused persons for or in connection with any demand of dowry.
The statements of PW-1, PW-2 and PW-3 recorded before the then SDM, Dwarka also fail to prove the said essential requirement of offence of dowry death as defined under Section 304-B IPC.

Even otherwise, as held above, the prosecution has miserably failed to proved on record that any dowry demands were made by any of the accused persons from deceased Harnesh or she was subjected to cruelty or harassment for fulfillment of the said dowry demands.

In the absence of evidence to this effect, it is difficult to presume that the State vs Jai Prakash on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83141473/
9 suicide of deceased Harnesh was in fact a dowry death or that any of the accused persons were responsible for the same.

48.In these circumstances, all the essential ingredients required to be proved before presumption of dowry death can be drawn u/s 304B r/w Section 113B Evidence Act,1872 have not been duly proved on record beyond any reasonable doubt.
Since, the prosecution has failed to prove on record the basic ingredients of Section 304B IPC, no occasion arises for drawing the presumption of dowry death as mandated u/s 113B Indian Evidence Act.
Thus, both the accused persons namely Jai Prakash @ Dev Prakash and Banke Lal are entitled to acquittal for offence u/s 304B/34 IPC.

CONCLUSION/FINDINGS:
49.In view of the detailed reasons given above and considering the overall evidence produced on record
, both the accused persons namely Jai Prakash @ Dev Prakash and Banke Lal are acquitted for offences u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC as charged against them giving them the benefit of doubt.
50. File be consigned to record room after due compliance.
SHIVALI by SHIVALI SHARMA Announced in the open court

23.
In the present case, accused persons are charged with the offences u/s 498A/304B/34 IPC.
24.
In order to bring home the charge of dowry death u/s 304B IPC, it is essential for the prosecution to prove the following ingredients:
(a) that the death of the woman was caused by any burns or bodily injuries or in the circumstances which are not normal;
(b) such death occurs within seven years from the date of marriage;
(c) that the victim was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of the husband;
(d) such cruelty or harassment should be for or in connection with the demand of dowry; and (e) it is established that such cruelty or harassment was made soon before her death.
28. Section 304B IPC works on the concept of deeming fiction which is hardly applicable to criminal jurisdiction.
Accordingly, where other ingredients of Section 304B IPC are satisfied, the husband or the relative shall be deemed to have caused the death of the lady.
In other words, the offence shall be deemed to have been committed by fiction of law.
Once the prosecution proves its case with regard to the basic ingredients of Section 304B IPC, the court will presume by deemed fiction of law that the husbands or the relatives complained of, have caused her death.
Such a presumption can be drawn by the court, keeping in view the evidence produced by the prosecution in support of the substantive charge u/s 304B IPC.

The soul of Section 34 IPC is the joint liability of doing a criminal act.
This section only provides a rule of evidence and does not create a substantive offence.
Two elements are necessary to fulfill the requirement of Section 34 IPC.
One is that the person must be present on the scene of occurrence and the second is that there must be a prior concert or a pre- arranged plan.
Unless these two conditions are fulfilled, a person cannot be held guilty of an offence by operation of Section 34 IPC.
33.
Common intention implies a pre-arranged plan and acting in concert pursuance to that plan.
Common intention comes into being prior to the commission of act in point of time which need not be a long gap.
The common intention to give effect to a particular act may even develop at the spur of the moment between a number of persons with reference to the facts of a given case.
Where there is no direct evidence of common intention, it has to be inferred from circumstantial evidence.
When the factum of dowry demands is not duly proved on record, the harassment of the deceased with a view to coerce her or any of her parental family members to meet the unlawful dowry demands have also not been proved on record beyond any reasonable doubt.
Neither the demands of dowry are duly proved on record, nor it is proved on record that the harassment given to deceased Harnesh was of such a nature as was likely to drive her to commit suicide or to cause grave injury to her life, limb or health.
Although, deceased Harnesh has committed suicide as per medical evidence, however, the evidence on record is highly deficient for holding that it was because of the cruelty suffered by her at the hands of any of the accused persons.
48.In these circumstances, all the essential ingredients required to be proved before presumption of dowry death can be drawn u/s 304B r/w Section 113B Evidence Act,1872 have not been duly proved on record beyond any reasonable doubt.
Since, the prosecution has failed to prove on record the basic ingredients of Section 304B IPC, no occasion arises for drawing the presumption of dowry death as mandated u/s 113B Indian Evidence Act.
